correctness.rationale: The orthonormal local basis \(u=(i,1)^T/\sqrt2,\ v=(-i,1)^T/\sqrt2\) converts the hopping block to \(J|u\rangle\langle v|\) and the onsite \(\sigma_z\) term to -(|u><v|+|v><u|). This yields the stated invariant blocks. The \(3\times3\), \(4\times4\), and \(6\times6\) determinant recurrences give the three displayed characteristic polynomials. The \(P_4\) discriminant is negative for \(0<\gamma<4J\); at the central position the projected perturbation on the \(+J\) eigenspace has eigenvalues \(0,\pm i\gamma/(2\sqrt2)\); at the edge position the moving roots stay real up to \(\gamma=2J\) and become imaginary beyond it. The standard-library checker passed 56 matrix-transform cases and the three block determinant recurrences.

value.rationale: The exact classification isolates a physically natural finite-size invariant: the first PT-breaking threshold as the balanced pair moves from the ends into the bulk. It gives a closed-form characteristic polynomial for every even length and every mirror-pair position, replaces large-matrix diagonalization with blocks of dimension at most six, and explains the sharp contrast between a protected edge pair and immediately unstable interior pairs at the Majorana dimerization point. This is a complete parameter-position classification, not merely a finite numerical census.
